title: Canonical restriction units on nested subspaces and under isomorphisms
statement: Let $Z$ be a topological space, $G$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $Z$, and $E\subseteq Z$ any subset with the subspace topology. Write $e:E\hookrightarrow Z$ for inclusion and $G_E=e^{-1}G$, with inverse image and units as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. For an open $V\subseteq Z$ containing $E$, let $v:V\hookrightarrow Z$ and $p_V:E\hookrightarrow V$ be inclusions and define $r_V:G(V)\to G_E(E)$ to be the unit $\eta^e_{G,V}$, identifying $e^{-1}V=E$. Then $v^{-1}G$ is canonically isomorphic to ordinary restriction $G|_V$, with the unit equal to ordinary restriction on every open. There is exactly one ring-sheaf isomorphism $c_V:p_V^{-1}(G|_V)\xrightarrow{\sim}e^{-1}G$ (the canonical composition isomorphism) such that $c_{V,E\cap B}\bigl(\eta^{p_V}_{G|_V,B}(s)\bigr)=\eta^e_{G,B}(s)$ for every open $B\subseteq V$ and every $s\in G(B)$; for $B=V$ this identifies the composite of the two inverse-image units with $r_V$. For $E\subseteq W\subseteq V$ with $W,V$ open, the transition obtained by inverse-image unit and canonical composition on $G(V)$ is ordinary restriction to $G(W)$, and $$r_W\circ\operatorname{res}_{V,W}=r_V.$$ The same composition and restriction identifications hold for sheaves of sets, with the canonical set composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-composition]. Moreover, let $g:Z\to Z'$ be a homeomorphism, let $G'$ be a commutative-ring sheaf on $Z'$, and let $\theta:G'\xrightarrow{\sim}g_*G$ be a ring-sheaf isomorphism. Put $E'=g(E)$, $g_E:E\to E'$, and $e':E'\hookrightarrow Z'$. There is a unique ring-sheaf isomorphism $\theta_E:e'^{-1}G'\xrightarrow{\sim}(g_E)_*e^{-1}G$ characterized, on every open $B'\subseteq Z'$, by $$\theta_E\circ\eta^{e'}_{G',B'}=\eta^e_{G,g^{-1}B'}\circ\theta_{B'},$$ with components evaluated on $E'\cap B'$ and identified via $g_E$. Consequently, writing $g_E^\sharp=\theta_E(E')$ and $g_V^\sharp=\theta_{g(V)}$, one has $$g_E^\sharp\circ r'_{g(V)}=r_V\circ g_V^\sharp$$ for every open $V$ containing $E$. Empty subspaces and empty opens are allowed.

proof.text: Work simultaneously for a coefficient category satisfying the concrete sheafification hypotheses, then specialize to CommRingCat and Type. Transport the abstract inverse-image unit across the canonical isomorphism with the sheafified left Kan extension, using the proved source-library formula Functor.sheafAdjunctionContinuous_unit_app_hom_sheafPullbackIso_hom. Unfold the open-embedding comparison: sheafification naturality cancels its lifts, and the pointwise left Kan extension universal property identifies the canonical coprojection with the ordinary restriction map. This proves exactly the unit equation for Mathlib's sheafPullbackIso, not merely for an arbitrary open-restriction isomorphism.

Transport the open-inclusion adjunction along sheafPullbackIso and compose it with the adjunction for p_V. Its right adjoint is definitionally the direct image for e. Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq supplies c_V and its composite-unit equation. Evaluate on the ambient image of an open B of V. Naturality along the unit B → v⁻¹v(B) of the opens adjunction, and its triangle identity, turn the composite-unit equation into the stated equation for B. Injectivity of the p_V adjunction hom bijection proves uniqueness for the fixed G. Taking B = top and applying unit naturality along v(top) → V gives the global section formula. The identical generic construction proves the set-valued statement, with the same unit characterization as the canonical set composition isomorphism; no separate set-composition theorem is needed.

Apply naturality of the inverse-image unit for e to W ≤ V and then restrict to the whole subspace E. Functoriality of restriction combines the lower maps and gives r_W res_(V,W) = r_V. This argument works for both rings and sets.

Lift the presheaf equivalences induced by the homeomorphisms g and g_E to equivalences T and S of sheaf categories. At every ambient open, direct images e_* ⋙ T and S ⋙ e'_* evaluate on the same inverse-image open, giving an identity-component natural isomorphism beta between them.

Take the inverse mate alpha of beta for the inverse-image adjunctions of e and e'. The proved library theorem isIso_inverseMate_of_equivalences makes alpha invertible. Define theta_E as the composite of e'⁻¹(theta) with alpha_G. The inverse-mate unit identity and naturality of the e' unit under theta give the required unit square on every ambient open. Injectivity of the e' adjunction hom bijection proves uniqueness among isomorphisms with this square.

Evaluate the unit square at g(V) and restrict along E' → e'⁻¹g(V). Naturality of theta_E moves this restriction across the comparison. Naturality of the e unit along V → g⁻¹g(V), followed by functoriality of restriction, gives the required global section equation. All equalities of open-set morphisms follow from their subsingleton hom sets. No point, section, nonempty open, or nonempty subspace is chosen.
